quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The bakery on Elm Street opens at five in the morning, long before most shops. By then, the owner has already been up for three hours, shaping dough and lighting the oven. Bus drivers, nurses, and night-shift workers line up for warm rolls. The bread is good, but many customers say they come for the quiet, friendly start to their day.
options: How Small Shops Compete with Supermarkets
The Bakery That Serves Early Risers and Shift Workers
The Importance of a Good Breakfast
quests.correctAnswer: The Bakery That Serves Early Risers and Shift Workers
quests.hint: The owner is up before the customers are. Ask which idea covers both the owner and the customers.
quests.explanation: Shaping dough is one detail, and breakfast in general is too wide. The passage is about a bakery whose hours and atmosphere suit people who start work early.
quests.whyThisTitle: The owner's early start and the line of early-shift customers both describe a bakery built around early risers.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Last year the city placed 300 shared bicycles at stations across downtown. Riders unlock a bike with a phone and return it to any station. Most trips are under twenty minutes, and many riders use the bikes to reach the train. Officials say the bikes have cut short car trips in the center.
options: Riding a Bike to the Train Station
Unlocking a Bike with Your Phone at a Station
Solving Traffic Problems in Big Cities
quests.correctAnswer: Bike Sharing and City Travel
quests.hint: Several details are given. Which choice could hold all of them together?
quests.explanation: Phone unlocking and train connections are both details inside a larger picture of how the bikes are used. A title about traffic in big cities goes far beyond one downtown scheme.
quests.whyThisTitle: The best title covers the stations, the short trips, and the train links as parts of one system, without over-stretching to all traffic problems.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Mei joined the school orchestra because a friend asked her to. For weeks she sat at the back and barely spoke. Then the conductor gave her a short solo, and the audience clapped loudly at the concert. Mei now speaks up in rehearsals, and she has started helping younger players.
options: Joining a Club to Please a Friend
quests.correctAnswer: How the Orchestra Changed Mei
quests.hint: Look at how Mei is described at the beginning and at the end.
quests.explanation: The solo is the turning point, but the passage covers the change before and after it. The best title reflects the whole change in Mei.
quests.whyThisTitle: The shy start, the solo, and her new confidence together show what the orchestra did for Mei.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The school cafeteria replaced its fried options with grilled chicken, soup, and a salad bar last term. At first, sales dropped, and some students complained. After a month, the cooks added tasty sauces and let students vote on new dishes. Now lunch sales are higher than before.
options: Voting on the Next New Dish
quests.correctAnswer: Making a Healthier Menu Popular
quests.hint: The passage changes direction partway through. Which title fits the beginning and the end?
quests.explanation: Complaints and voting are stages in the story, and healthy eating in general is much wider. The passage covers a menu change and how students came to accept it.
quests.whyThisTitle: It captures both the unpopular start and the successful outcome, not just one stage.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: When the power went out on Tuesday, the whole street went dark. Neighbors came outside with flashlights, and someone brought a small stove to heat soup. Children played cards by candlelight while adults shared news about how long repairs might take. When the lights returned at ten, people were almost sorry the evening was over.
options: How an Outage United a Street
quests.correctAnswer: How an Outage United a Street
quests.hint: Notice how people feel at the end. What does that feeling say about the evening?
quests.explanation: The card games and the repair news are details. The final sentence shows what the evening really meant to the neighbors.
quests.whyThisTitle: The gathering, the shared soup, and the reluctant ending all show how the outage connected the neighbors.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: New workers at the distribution center spend their first three days in training. They learn how to lift boxes safely, read shipping labels, and use the handheld scanner. On the fourth day, each person is paired with an experienced coworker. Managers say the pairing helps new staff more than any handout.
options: How New Warehouse Workers Learn Their Jobs
Learning to Use a Handheld Scanner
Why Safety Matters in Every Job
quests.correctAnswer: How New Warehouse Workers Learn Their Jobs
quests.hint: Ask which choice covers both the classroom days and the fourth day.
quests.explanation: The scanner lesson and the coworker pairing are both parts of the training. Only one option covers the entire process.
quests.whyThisTitle: The title includes the three days of instruction and the paired work that follows.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Ferries to Kelly Island run every hour in summer but only three times a day in winter. Tickets can be bought at the dock or online, and cars must be booked in advance. The crossing takes forty minutes, and the upper deck is the best place to watch for seabirds. Visitors who miss the last boat must stay the night.
options: Booking a Car Space in Advance
Planning a Ferry Trip to the Island
Watching Seabirds from the Upper Deck
quests.correctAnswer: Planning a Ferry Trip to the Island
quests.hint: Every detail here would matter to someone getting ready to go. Who is the passage for?
quests.explanation: Timetables, tickets, car booking, and the last boat are all things a traveler must plan around. The seabirds and the car booking are single details.
quests.whyThisTitle: The schedules, ticket options, and last-boat warning all belong to preparing a ferry trip.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Sana read her history chapter three times and still could not remember it. Her teacher suggested a different approach: close the book and write down everything she could recall. Sana was surprised at how much she had forgotten, but the gaps showed her exactly what to review. After two weeks of this, her quiz scores rose.
options: Simple Ways to Get Better Grades
Preparing for Weekly Quizzes in History Class
Reading a Difficult History Chapter Three Times
quests.correctAnswer: Recalling Instead of Rereading
quests.hint: Compare the two study methods the passage describes. Which one does it favor?
quests.explanation: Rereading is the method that fails, so a title about it points the wrong way. The passage is about switching to recall and seeing results.
quests.whyThisTitle: This title names the new method and implies the contrast with rereading that the story is built on.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: A tool library lets residents borrow drills, ladders, and garden shears for a small yearly fee. Most people need such tools only a few times a year, so buying them is costly and takes up storage space. Volunteers repair items and teach basic skills on Saturdays. Members say the library has saved them money and introduced them to neighbors.
options: Saving Money on Everyday Home Repairs
Borrowing Tools Instead of Buying Them
Keeping Ladders and Drills in Good Shape
quests.correctAnswer: Borrowing Tools Instead of Buying Them
quests.hint: Ask what problem the borrowing service solves, and what the extras are.
quests.explanation: Weekend repairs and money saved are side benefits. The main point is the choice between borrowing and buying.
quests.whyThisTitle: The yearly fee, the reasons not to buy, and the volunteer help all support the idea of borrowing.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Tourists at Green Hill Farm feed goats in the morning, collect eggs, and help make cheese in the afternoon. Nights are spent in simple wooden cabins without television. The owners started the stays when milk prices fell, and the extra income now pays for new equipment. Guests leave with sore arms and many stories.
options: Overnight Guests on a Working Farm
quests.correctAnswer: Overnight Guests on a Working Farm
quests.hint: Which choice explains both what guests do and why the farm offers it?
quests.explanation: Cheese making and cabins are only two of many guest activities. The passage also explains why the owners began the stays.
quests.whyThisTitle: Guest activities and the reason for starting them both fit under the idea of a farm welcoming visitors.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Good speakers are not afraid of silence. A short pause before an important point makes listeners lean forward. A pause after a question gives the audience time to think. Nervous speakers often rush through these moments, filling them with 'um' and 'uh,' and the message loses its force.
options: Using Pauses to Strengthen a Speech
Asking Good Questions in a Presentation
quests.correctAnswer: Using Pauses to Strengthen a Speech
quests.hint: What is the one technique that every example in the passage returns to?
quests.explanation: Fillers, nerves, and questions are all mentioned but only in relation to pausing. The technique itself is the central idea.
quests.whyThisTitle: The pause before a point, the pause after a question, and the cost of rushing all concern pausing.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Because of signal repairs, trains between Lakeside and Central Station will run every thirty minutes instead of every ten this weekend. Passengers should expect longer waits, especially on Sunday afternoon. Extra staff will be on the platforms to answer questions, and the cafeteria at Central will stay open late. Normal service returns Monday at 5:00 a.m.
options: Signal Repairs Between Lakeside and Central
quests.correctAnswer: Weekend Train Delays
quests.hint: Ask what a traveler most needs to know after reading this notice.
quests.explanation: The repairs explain why the delays happen, but the notice is mostly about what passengers will experience. Extra staff is a single supporting detail.
quests.whyThisTitle: The changed frequency, the busiest time, and the return date all concern the weekend delays.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Every year, fifth graders present science projects in the school gym. Some build small volcanoes, while others test which paper towel soaks up the most water. Judges care less about flashy displays than about whether the student asked a clear question and tested it fairly. The winner this year compared three brands of batteries.
options: Judges' Priorities at a Science Fair
Why Children Enjoy Science Experiments at School
quests.correctAnswer: Judges' Priorities at a Science Fair
quests.hint: The examples are only illustrations. Ask what the people doing the judging care about most.
quests.explanation: Volcanoes and batteries are examples of projects. The passage's point is what the judges reward.
quests.whyThisTitle: This choice links the examples to the judges' real standard: a clear question and a fair test.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: On the first Sunday of each month, the city museum opens for free. Lines can stretch around the block by ten in the morning, so many visitors arrive early. Families often use the free day to explore the dinosaur hall, while students sketch in the art rooms. Regular visitors say the quieter afternoon hours are the best time to go.
options: Making the Most of Free Museum Day
The High Cost of Visiting a City Museum
quests.correctAnswer: Making the Most of Free Museum Day
quests.hint: Ask what the passage helps a reader do.
quests.explanation: The dinosaur hall and the art rooms are examples of how people spend the day. The passage as a whole gives guidance on when and how to visit.
quests.whyThisTitle: The crowd warning, the popular activities, and the quieter-hours tip are all advice for a better visit.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Teenagers often stay awake late and struggle to wake for school. Researchers point out that a teenager's body clock naturally shifts later during these years, so early classes ask students to be alert before their brains are ready. Some schools that moved the start time by an hour saw fewer students arriving late and fewer nodding off in class.
options: Ways Teenagers Waste Time Late at Night
Fewer Late Arrivals After a Later Bell
Why Teenagers Struggle with Early Morning Classes
quests.correctAnswer: Why Teenagers Struggle with Early Morning Classes
quests.hint: Look for the explanation the passage gives, not just the results.
quests.explanation: The late-arrival numbers are evidence, and the passage says the problem comes from the body clock, not from laziness. The title should point to the problem and its cause.
quests.whyThisTitle: The best title reflects the mismatch between teens' body clocks and early classes, which the whole passage develops.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: In a mountain village, a group of farmers formed a cooperative to sell their coffee together. Alone, each had to accept the low price offered by traders. As a group, they could store beans, find buyers abroad, and negotiate better prices. Members now earn more, and the village school has a new roof.
options: A New Roof for the Village School
Global Coffee Trade and Its Prices
Storing Coffee Beans in the Mountains
quests.correctAnswer: How Farmers Gained Strength Together
quests.hint: Ask what changed when the farmers stopped acting alone.
quests.explanation: The school roof is one result, and the global trade is much larger than this village. The center of the passage is the benefit of joining together.
quests.whyThisTitle: Every benefit listed comes from acting as a group instead of as individuals.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: After the city painted a red lane on Harbor Road for buses only, trips that once took thirty-five minutes now take twenty-two. Drivers of private cars complained at first about losing a lane. However, more commuters switched to the bus, and traffic for cars has eased slightly as well. The city plans to add similar lanes on two more roads.
options: Traffic Problems in Cities Around the World
How a Bus-Only Lane Sped Up Trips on Harbor Road
quests.correctAnswer: How a Bus-Only Lane Sped Up Trips on Harbor Road
quests.hint: Which title covers the change, the objection, and the outcome?
quests.explanation: The complaints are an early reaction, and painting lanes is only how the change was made. The passage follows the effect of the bus lane.
quests.whyThisTitle: It captures the faster trips and the broader effects the passage reports.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Reading aloud to young children builds more than a love of stories. Children hear new words they might not meet in everyday talk. They also learn how sentences are shaped and how a story moves from beginning to end. Teachers say children who are read to regularly start school with an advantage.
options: How Schools Prepare Children for Class
Benefits Children Gain from Being Read To
quests.correctAnswer: Benefits Children Gain from Being Read To
quests.hint: Look at what the passage says children get, not at who does the reading.
quests.explanation: New words, sentence patterns, and story shape are all benefits. Nothing in the passage is about choosing books or learning to read independently.
quests.whyThisTitle: Vocabulary, sentence sense, and story structure together are what children gain.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The Rex Cinema had been closed for ten years when a group of residents decided to save it. They raised money through bake sales, asked local firms to repair the roof, and painted the walls themselves. When it reopened last spring, the first film sold out in an hour. The Rex now shows old classics on Mondays and new releases the rest of the week.
options: Neighbors Work Together to Rescue an Old Cinema
quests.correctAnswer: Neighbors Work Together to Rescue an Old Cinema
quests.hint: Ask who did the work and what the result was.
quests.explanation: Bake sales and Monday films are small details. The passage tells a story of restoration by neighbors.
quests.whyThisTitle: The fundraising, the repairs, and the sold-out reopening all show a cinema being revived.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: A laptop's processor, memory, and storage all affect speed, but the right combination depends on the person. Someone who only writes documents and browses the web will not notice the difference between a basic model and an expensive one. A video editor, though, needs a stronger processor and more memory. Deciding what you will do with the laptop should come before comparing prices.
options: Matching a Laptop to Your Needs
Why Video Editors Need Fast Computers
quests.correctAnswer: Matching a Laptop to Your Needs
quests.hint: Ask what the writer wants you to decide first.
quests.explanation: Video editing and memory are examples used to make a point. The passage advises basing the choice on your own needs.
quests.whyThisTitle: The two example users illustrate the advice to choose according to purpose.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Volunteers at the animal shelter do more than play with puppies. They clean cages, walk dogs, and take photos for the adoption website. The photos matter more than expected: shelters report that animals with clear, cheerful pictures leave faster. A few volunteers have become full-time staff.
options: The Many Jobs of Shelter Volunteers
Taking Photos That Help Pets Get Adopted
Adopting a Puppy from a Shelter
quests.correctAnswer: The Many Jobs of Shelter Volunteers
quests.hint: One detail gets extra attention. Ask whether it is the whole passage or one job among several.
quests.explanation: Photography gets a whole sentence of praise, but it is still one of three jobs. The opening sentence signals that the passage is about the range of tasks.
quests.whyThisTitle: Cleaning, walking, and photographing are all jobs volunteers do, so the title should cover the range.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: As the sun sets, the parking lot near the river becomes a night market. Stalls sell grilled corn, secondhand books, and phone cases, while a man in a red hat repairs shoes on the spot. Prices are lower than in stores, and bargaining is expected. For many visitors, the noise, the smell of frying, and the crowds are part of the pleasure.
quests.correctAnswer: Night Market Comes Alive
quests.hint: Ask what experience the writer is trying to capture.
quests.explanation: The passage lists goods, prices, and atmosphere. The final sentence shows that the overall experience is the point.
quests.whyThisTitle: The stalls, the bargaining, and the noise all add up to the experience of the market at night.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Every Monday, Ms. Reyes asks her team one question: what is getting in your way? She does not ask for a report or a list of achievements. The answers vary: a broken printer, an unclear request, a missing password. Because problems are raised early, they are usually fixed before they slow anyone down.
options: Why Leading a Team Is Difficult
Clearing Obstacles with One Weekly Question
quests.correctAnswer: Clearing Obstacles with One Weekly Question
quests.hint: Look at why the question is asked and what it produces.
quests.explanation: The printer and the password are examples of obstacles. The passage explains how one question helps the team.
quests.whyThisTitle: The question, the varied answers, and the early fixes all show a single management habit.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Fruit tastes best and costs less when it is in season. Strawberries sold in early summer are sweet and cheap, while winter ones may be pale and expensive because they have traveled a long way. Shoppers can check the price signs: a sudden drop usually means plenty is being harvested nearby. Buying what is in season also brings variety to the table across the year.
options: How Fruit Travels Around the World
The Sweetest Strawberries of Early Summer
Why Buying Seasonal Fruit Makes Sense
quests.correctAnswer: Why Buying Seasonal Fruit Makes Sense
quests.hint: Notice how many reasons are given for one choice.
quests.explanation: Strawberries, travel, and price signs appear as evidence or tips. The main claim is that seasonal buying is a good idea.
quests.whyThisTitle: Better taste, lower cost, and variety are all reasons that support the same choice.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: My grandfather repaired watches for forty years in a shop the size of a closet. He taught me to hold tiny screws with tweezers and to breathe slowly before touching a spring. I never became a watchmaker, but I still work the same way: patiently, one small part at a time. When my computer breaks, I hear his voice reminding me to breathe.
options: Repairing Watches in a Tiny Shop for Decades
quests.correctAnswer: Patience from a Watchmaker
quests.hint: The writer never became a watchmaker. So what did the grandfather leave behind?
quests.explanation: The shop is scene-setting, and the trade's decline is never discussed. The passage is about what the writer learned and still uses.
quests.whyThisTitle: The tweezers and breathing advice matter because they became a lasting way of working.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Near schools, speed limits drop to thirty kilometers an hour during arrival and departure times. Flashing signs remind drivers of the change, and crossing guards stop traffic when children need to cross. Drivers who ignore the limit can face heavy fines. Police say that most accidents involving children happen because of speed, not because of bad weather or poor roads.
options: Why Roads Are Dangerous in Bad Weather
quests.correctAnswer: Keeping Children Safe Near Schools
quests.hint: Look at what each measure is designed to protect.
quests.explanation: Fines and crossing guards are among several measures. The passage is about the whole set of protections for children.
quests.whyThisTitle: Lower limits, signs, guards, and fines all work toward protecting children on the road.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Ismail turned off nearly all the notifications on his phone. Now he hears a sound only for calls and messages from family. He checks email and social media three times a day, at times he chooses. In the first week he felt he was missing something. By the third week, he noticed he was finishing books again.
options: Taking Back Control from Phone Alerts
Checking Email and Social Media Three Times a Day
quests.correctAnswer: Taking Back Control from Phone Alerts
quests.hint: Ask who decides when Ismail looks at his phone before and after the change.
quests.explanation: Finishing books is a result, and the three daily checks are part of the method. The passage as a whole is about controlling interruptions.
quests.whyThisTitle: Silencing alerts and choosing check times both show him deciding when the phone gets his attention.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: In some countries people bow when they meet, in others they kiss on the cheek, and in others a warm handshake may last a while. A traveler may worry about doing the wrong thing. Most hosts, however, are forgiving, and a friendly smile and an effort to follow local habits are usually all that is needed.
options: How to Bow Politely When Meeting Someone
quests.correctAnswer: Greeting Customs for Travelers
quests.hint: The passage has a problem and a reassurance. Which title has room for both?
quests.explanation: Bowing is one custom, and nervousness is only the setup. The passage explains that greetings vary and that mistakes are usually forgiven.
quests.whyThisTitle: The title covers the variety of greetings and the guidance offered to travelers.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The school installed solar panels on its gym roof two years ago. On sunny days, they produce more power than the building uses, and the extra flows into the local grid. The savings pay for new library books. Students also study the data in science class, watching the numbers change with the weather.
options: Studying Weather Data in Science Class
How Solar Panels Benefit a School
Sending Extra Power to the Grid
quests.correctAnswer: How Solar Panels Benefit a School
quests.hint: Count the separate ways the school gains, and look for the title that holds them all.
quests.explanation: Grid sales and science lessons are separate benefits. Only one title includes everything, without drifting into general energy costs.
quests.whyThisTitle: Power, savings for books, and classroom learning are each ways the school benefits.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: A pharmacist does more than fill prescriptions. She checks whether a new medicine might react badly with something a patient already takes, explains when and how to take it, and answers questions people forget to ask their doctor. Many customers only realize her role when a problem is avoided. The counter is often the easiest place to get quick, reliable advice.
options: Why Doctors Are Hard to Reach
quests.correctAnswer: The Pharmacist's Real Role
quests.hint: The first sentence begins with 'more than.' What does that phrase promise?
quests.explanation: Interaction checks are one duty. The passage's point is that the pharmacist's role is wider than dispensing medicine.
quests.whyThisTitle: This title contrasts the obvious job with the several other things the pharmacist does.
